## 3. Route coverage

### Theme rows — 28 route instances

| Role | Routes checked | Count |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADMIN | `/dashboard`, `/schedules`, `/equipment`, `/ot-rooms`, `/doctors`, `/patients`, `/departments`, `/alerts`, `/users`, `/audit` | 10 |
| DOCTOR | `/dashboard`, `/schedules`, `/equipment`, `/ot-rooms`, `/doctors`, `/patients`, `/departments`, `/alerts` | 8 |
| OT_STAFF | `/dashboard`, `/schedules`, `/equipment`, `/ot-rooms`, `/doctors`, `/departments`, `/alerts` | 7 |
| PATIENT | `/dashboard`, `/patients/appointments`, `/alerts` | 3 |
| **Total** | | **28** |

For every row the harness recorded:

- the final pathname;
- body background;
- sidebar background;
- all visible elements whose computed background was darker than the approved light surfaces;
- shell presence and sidebar/header presence.

**Result:** 28 / 28 theme rows passed. Every page reported:

- body background `rgb(245, 248, 251)` (`#F5F8FB`);
- sidebar background `rgb(255, 255, 255)`;
- zero dark content surfaces;
- primary action `#245b8f`;
- shell and navigation present.

The full rows, including every sampled computed value, are in `evidence/browser-role-checks.json`.

### Authorization checks

| Role | Denied route attempted | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADMIN | `/patients/appointments` | `/unauthorized` |
| DOCTOR | `/users` | `/unauthorized` |
| OT_STAFF | `/patients` | `/unauthorized` |
| PATIENT | `/doctors` | `/unauthorized` |

The shared layout adds `requireAuth`, but it does not replace page-level `requireRole` / `requirePermission` checks. The denied routes prove those guards are still active.

### Sign-out

After each role sequence the harness signed out and checked:

1. the browser returned to `/login`;
2. no private shell remained in the DOM;
3. a private route request after sign-out did not render private content.

All three checks passed.

## 5. Persistent-shell evidence

For each role, the harness set unique DOM tokens on:

- `[data-app-shell]`;
- `[data-app-sidebar]`.

It then clicked sidebar destinations, used Back and Forward, and re-read those tokens.

Observed navigation counters:

| Role | Frame navigations during navigation sequence | Within-document navigations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADMIN | 0 | 9 |
| DOCTOR | 0 | 8 |
| OT_STAFF | 0 | 8 |
| PATIENT | 0 | 5 |

Every shell token was identical after every section change; every target pathname matched; every active navigation state was correct; no sidebar or history action produced a frame navigation.

The extra document loads in `eventCounts` belong to deliberate setup/reload steps (fresh role login, direct URL, refresh, screenshots), not to sidebar navigation.

### History and refresh

- Back returned to the previous section with the same shell subtree.
- Forward returned to the later section with the same shell subtree.
- Direct URLs loaded the requested route under the workspace layout.
- Refresh re-ran the server boundary and returned the same route. As expected, refresh creates a new document and therefore a new shell instance; this is distinct from client-side navigation.

| Command | Result | Log |

The production build compiled successfully and retained all authenticated routes, dynamic detail routes and permission-gated APIs.

`npx eslint src --max-warnings=0` over the entire source tree exits 1 on **17 pre-existing warnings** in `src/components/departments/DepartmentManagement.tsx` and `src/components/equipment/EquipmentManagement.tsx` (unused imports/locals). Those files were not modified in Stage 3C; the changed-file lint is clean. This is recorded as a known repository-wide warning baseline, not as a Stage 3C regression. See `evidence/lint-src-all.log`.

## 10. Console and network notes

The exhaustive role run recorded two transient console entries during its 74 setup document navigations:

- minified React error `#419`;
- `ChunkLoadError` for a chunk that was still loading when the harness moved to the next document.

A separate clean navigation run clicked five sidebar destinations with normal dwell time and recorded **zero console messages and zero network failures**. The detail-route run also recorded zero console exceptions.

The detail run recorded five canceled `Fetch` requests (`net::ERR_ABORTED`) caused by navigation while prefetch requests were in flight; no failed API response or route check was observed. These are reported as harness timing artifacts, not claimed as clean network traces.

## 11. Limitations

- The exhaustive test was run in Chrome only; Firefox and Safari were not tested.
- The loading skeleton, forced server error state and an empty seeded dataset were audited in source and share the same semantic tokens, but were not separately captured as screenshots. The schedule dialog, equipment form, populated tables, calendar and mobile layouts were exercised live.
- “No document navigation” is asserted for sidebar and history navigation. An explicit browser refresh and the schedule detail Refresh control intentionally create a new document.
- The harness was temporary and is not part of the application or test suite. Its raw JSON and logs are retained in `evidence/`.
- The role-run console entries in §10 are disclosed rather than suppressed; no route check failed because of them.
